# LuminalShine 26.10.1

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Bundled virtual display driver: LuminalVGD v0.1.0-alpha.9**  
> Signed driver **0.1.0.27** · protocol **0.10** · Build **27** — unchanged from 26.10.0 and 26.09.1.

LuminalShine **26.10.1** addresses two regressions reported in **26.10.0** when using **Exclusive mode with OLED Protection**: existing and newly opened applications could remain on physical displays instead of moving to the selected virtual display, and mouse interaction could expose content or a cursor on the protected physical displays. The report came from Aurora on LG webOS, with 26.09.1 identified as the last working release.

This maintenance release includes all fixes from [PR #211](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/211). The host-persisted WebUI changelog, VHF gamepad backend and Xbox Bluetooth Helper, encoder-probe fixes, and existing client connectivity features from [26.10.0](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/releases/tag/26.10.0) remain included.

## Virtual-display application routing

- **Restore periodic reconciliation.** A 500 ms sweep retries eligible windows that remain off the selected virtual display. This restores the periodic containment behavior from 26.09.1 while retaining exact-device targeting, covering missed or early window events, applications that restore saved monitor positions, and asynchronous moves that need another attempt.
- **Process queued window work promptly.** The desktop-guard worker now wakes for messages that Windows has already observed but not removed, and drains window work after configuration wakes as well as message wakes. Queued application moves no longer depend on a later unrelated event to resume processing.
- **Keep configuration and shutdown responsive.** A signaled configuration/shutdown event takes priority over continuous window input. Message draining is bounded, so a noisy application cannot indefinitely postpone reconfiguration.
- **Keep failed queue posts retryable.** Failed message posts release their pending entry. Periodic sweeps filter out windows already on the target so they do not consume the bounded routing queue ahead of off-target applications.
- **Retain exact-target safeguards.** Routing continues to use the session's selected VGD device, with configuration/topology generation checks and no fallback to an unrelated primary display. Maintenance timers are retired when configuration or topology changes.

## OLED Protection

- **Consume interaction on black covers.** Recovery-display covers now handle hit tests instead of forwarding mouse interaction to the applications beneath them. Clicking a cover does not activate it or the covered application.
- **Suppress the cursor over protected displays.** Cover cursor handling hides the pointer so hovering does not illuminate the physical display with a cursor.
- **Maintain the covers above application windows.** The periodic maintenance pass reasserts the covers' topmost position without activating them. Cover updates retain the generation barrier used during suspension and teardown.

## LuminalVGD driver

This fix is in LuminalShine's desktop helper; the bundled virtual **display** driver is unchanged:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Bundled release | **v0.1.0-alpha.9** |
| Driver version | **0.1.0.27** (`DriverVer 08/07/2026, 0.1.0.27`) |
| Protocol | **0.10** (handshake build 27, capabilities `0xfe5`) |
| Watchdog | 10-second lease watchdog |
| Signing | NortheBridge Foundation OV certificate, RFC 3161 timestamped |

Build 27 retains the D3D12 timeline-fence transport and teardown/drain protections. Upgrading from 26.10.0 does not normally require replacing this display driver. The separate VHF virtual gamepad package also remains unchanged: **v0.1.0-beta.9**, driver **0.1.0.53**, protocol **2**.

## Project, tests and release engineering

- Added six native Windows regression tests covering previously observed queued input, configuration-event priority, bounded message draining, shutdown, cover hit testing/no-activation, and cursor suppression.
- All **15 display-guard tests** (six native USER32 tests plus nine exact-device policy tests) are now part of the blocking Windows candidate/release gate. A focused Windows workflow runs them independently as well.
- Release validation passed **126 connection-path tests** and **72 frontend tests**. Its full Windows suite recorded **848 passed, 12 failed, and 10 skipped** (870 total), with no new failures versus 26.10.0. The 12 existing failures are an authentication error-text expectation, eight Playnite tests, and three locale-consistency tests. This is not an all-tests-green release.
- **Release CI results** ([run](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/actions/runs/40609903325)): signing, signed-payload integrity, MSI upgrade compatibility, installer invariants, GameStream health checks, the connection/display-guard gate, and configuration consistency all passed. The release is built from commit `dba21a9ef69222b40a18227c2783853b954dfdf7`.
- The changes do not alter the networking protocols, authentication, encoder selection, or capture-start logic. Automated tests validate the routing and cover mechanisms and connection policies; they do not substitute for physical multi-monitor, Aurora/LG OLED, or other client hardware testing.

## Upgrading

- Install **26.10.1** over the previous release with the installer. Settings and pairings are retained; an active stream ends during the upgrade and can be restarted after the service returns.
- For the reported configuration, reconnect Aurora using **Exclusive mode with OLED Protection enabled**. Check both already-open and newly launched applications on the selected virtual display, then verify the physical displays stay covered during mouse movement and after reconnecting.
- Hard-refresh Mission Control (`Ctrl+F5`) if old assets remain cached. Use **Changelog** in navigation to reopen these notes.
- Regular Moonlight sessions, Borealis compatibility, the browser **Play** page, and opt-in PyroWave support remain available through their existing paths.


The same hashes are attached as **SHA256SUMS**.

# LuminalShine 26.10.0

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Bundled virtual display driver: LuminalVGD v0.1.0-alpha.9**  
> Signed driver **0.1.0.27** · protocol **0.10** · Build **27** — unchanged from 26.10.0-beta.1 and 26.09.1.

LuminalShine **26.10.0 Gold** adds a host-persisted WebUI changelog, replaces the ViGEm gamepad backend with Nonary's VHF virtual gamepad driver, and fixes an encoder-probe inconsistency that could prevent streaming even when the requested codec worked. These notes cover the packaging baseline at `e2662a44` through the Gold release commit. The PyroWave, Borealis compatibility, pairing, and reconnect improvements introduced in [26.10.0-beta.1](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/releases/tag/26.10.0-beta.1) remain included; WebRTC remains enabled in the Windows build.

## Changelog in Mission Control

- **New Update Available!** The WebUI displays eligible newer releases with their notes and a download link. Prerelease visibility follows the host's existing update-notification setting.
- **Read the installed release once per user and host.** On the first authenticated visit for an unseen installed version, a **Changelog** screen shows that version's notes. The acknowledgement is saved on the LuminalShine host, so it survives browser storage clearing, another browser, restarts, and normal upgrades. Reading a newer release before installing it does not mark the installed-version notes as read.
- **Open and close the changelog whenever needed.** Desktop navigation and the mobile menu provide access to release history. Notes are acknowledged only after content renders; unavailable notes are not marked as read.
- **Featurebase and GitHub stay connected.** Published GitHub releases are imported into Featurebase as drafts, with matching based on the dedicated original-release citation ([#207](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/207), [#208](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/208)). Release timestamps are reconciled, and a public changelog feed supplies the WebUI. Until a corresponding Featurebase update is published, the feed uses the public GitHub release notes. Cached notes support offline reading.

## VHF virtual gamepads and Xbox Bluetooth Helper

- **New virtual gamepad backend.** LuminalShine now uses Nonary's `libvirtualgamepad` UMDF/VHF driver, as implemented in Vibepollo, instead of ViGEmBus. The pinned package is **v0.1.0-beta.9**, driver **0.1.0.53**, protocol **2**; it requires x64 Windows 10 version 2004/build 19041 or newer, including Windows 11.
- **Controller recovery and feedback.** The backend preserves controller input, battery state, and supported feedback during recovery. DualShock 4 maintenance retains report cadence and gyro-stream recovery. Mission Control exposes the new driver health and controller profiles.
- **Xbox Bluetooth Helper follows the new backend.** The opt-in helper detects physical Bluetooth Xbox arrivals and briefly creates a VHF controller to trigger XInput enumeration. Allocation is coordinated with streaming and recovery to avoid competing for controller slots.
- **Signed driver packaging.** Release CI verifies the pinned package and signs its catalog and setup executable with the LuminalShine release identity. Installation validates the package and signer. Where needed for unattended installation, it enrolls that verified production signing certificate in Windows' machine-wide TrustedPublisher store; this also trusts other packages signed by that certificate. `INSTALL_VHF_GAMEPAD=0` skips the MSI driver action and publisher enrollment.
- **Shared drivers are retained.** A compatible driver installed by Vibepollo can be reused; equal/newer active drivers and newer staged packages are preserved. ViGEmBus is not removed because other applications may still need it. The shared VHF driver remains installed when LuminalShine is uninstalled.

See the [virtual gamepad driver guide](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/blob/a99282544d1612310514b0e8e4ccba587adc1028/docs/virtual-gamepad-driver.md) for installation, signing behavior, portable setup, and troubleshooting.

## Encoder probing and connection reliability

- **A failed codec no longer invalidates working codecs** ([#210](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/210), issue [#209](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/issues/209)). Failed HEVC or AV1 validation now clears stale capability flags. Previously, those flags could make the isolated video worker reject the entire encoder snapshot, including sessions requesting working H.264 or HEVC.
- **Codec settings invalidate the probe cache.** Changing HEVC or AV1 mode forces a fresh probe instead of reusing capability results from the previous settings.
- **Clearer startup diagnostics.** Rejected encoder snapshots and worker-start messages record specific reasons, with logs flushed before the worker exits. Successful startup paths and network protocols are unchanged.
- **Hardware limitation.** The issue report was identified and the PR was merged for 26.10.0 Gold, but no RTX 4080 was available to reproduce or verify the reported GPU-specific failure. Snapshot tests validate consistency; they do not substitute for hardware streaming tests.

Thanks to **[@magalz](https://github.com/magalz)** for the encoder-probe fix and diagnostics, and **[Nonary](https://github.com/Nonary)** for the virtual gamepad implementation.

## LuminalVGD driver

The virtual **display** driver is separate from the new virtual **gamepad** driver. This release retains the same LuminalVGD package:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Bundled release | **v0.1.0-alpha.9** |
| Driver version | **0.1.0.27** (`DriverVer 08/07/2026, 0.1.0.27`) |
| Protocol | **0.10** (handshake build 27, capabilities `0xfe5`) |
| Watchdog | 10-second lease watchdog |
| Signing | NortheBridge Foundation OV certificate, RFC 3161 timestamped |

Build 27 retains the D3D12 timeline-fence transport and teardown/drain protections. Upgrading from 26.09.1 or 26.10.0-beta.1 does not normally require replacing this display driver.

## Project, tests and release engineering

- The packaging baseline ([#206](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/206), `e2662a44`) explicitly retains the optional libatomic runtime and recognizes truncated Vue content hashes in MSI upgrade checks.
- Release CI pins the build timestamp across CMake reconfiguration so packaging does not rebuild already-signed executables.
- Release validation corrected the gamepad probe to pass the owning input handle, fixing a Windows compiler error in the VHF integration.
- New coverage includes host changelog acknowledgements, the public feed and WebUI behavior, VHF controller policy and recovery, Bluetooth-helper coordination, signed-package validation, publisher-enrollment rollback, and MSI compatibility.
- **Release CI results** ([run](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/actions/runs/40251737464)): signing, signed-payload integrity, MSI compatibility, installer invariants, GameStream readiness self-tests, PyroWave/connection-path tests, and configuration consistency passed. The advisory suite recorded **842 passed, 12 failed, and 10 skipped** (864 total). The 12 failures exactly match the beta baseline: an authentication error-text expectation, eight Playnite tests, and three locale-consistency tests. All new changelog state, VHF policy/recovery/maintenance, Xbox helper, and encoder snapshot tests passed. This is not an all-tests-green release.
- Windows release CI builds the installer, portable archive, and debug symbols; signing and packaging checks must pass before publication. Hardware driver loading, Bluetooth reconnect, and GPU streaming require validation on a Windows host.

## Upgrading

- Install **26.10.0** over the previous release with the installer. Settings and pairings are retained; an active stream ends during the upgrade and can be restarted after the service returns.
- Check the WebUI's gamepad driver status after installation, and restart Windows if requested. Driver installation errors are logged without rolling back the application; a working VHF driver is required for virtual gamepad input.
- Portable users can install the bundled gamepad driver using elevated 64-bit PowerShell as described in the driver guide.
- Hard-refresh Mission Control (`Ctrl+F5`) if old assets remain cached. Use **Changelog** in navigation to reopen these notes.
- PyroWave remains experimental and opt-in with a compatible client. WebRTC remains available from the **Play** page; regular Moonlight sessions continue to negotiate H.264, HEVC, or AV1.

## Checksums

SHA-256:

```text
178b8fe2d95d0e8e217a968f08f4d976ff0bb3349aedac56518c1cba1af23644  LuminalShine_x64-debuginfo.7z
b770a0143cc1e1c8b674959ad3e85241500a8e3c347a24a10983252c5101f36c  LuminalShine_x64-installer.exe
78041f1dc85cfc495382060e612c896f7ad78eac183775b5e045bbef1116bf16  LuminalShine_x64-portable.zip
```

The same hashes are attached as **SHA256SUMS**.

**Changes since the beta packaging baseline:** [`e2662a44…a9928254`](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/compare/e2662a44f8533df85dad163c4e947945e67d7fcd...a99282544d1612310514b0e8e4ccba587adc1028)

# LuminalShine 26.10.0-beta.1

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Bundled virtual display driver: LuminalVGD v0.1.0-alpha.9**  
> Signed driver **0.1.0.27** · protocol **0.10** · Build **27** — unchanged from 26.09.1.

LuminalShine 26.10.0-beta.1 introduces **experimental PyroWave SDR and HDR streaming in the official Windows build**, improves pairing and reconnect reliability, and fixes compatibility with **Borealis**, an Android client based on Moonlight and tuned for LuminalShine. This prerelease also adds exact virtual-display window routing, trusted application-library imports, clearer Mission Control status, and refreshed documentation. **WebRTC remains enabled and its runtime is included in the Windows packages.**

## PyroWave joins the official Windows build

- **Experimental SDR and HDR10 streaming** ([#187](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/187), [#192](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/192), [#193](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/193)). PyroWave supports SDR BT.709 and HDR10 BT.2020/PQ with 4:2:0 and 4:4:4 profiles. The Windows release now compiles the codec and its shaders, with a default compressed-video target of **700 Mbps**.
- **Built in, but opt-in.** Enable experimental PyroWave in Advanced settings and use a compatible client. The host advertises only profiles that pass its bounded availability probe; H.264, HEVC and AV1 retain their existing negotiation paths. Stock Moonlight clients continue to select a regular codec.
- **GPU capture integration.** PyroWave imports host-owned D3D11 textures on the matching Vulkan adapter without uncompressed CPU readback. HDR capture is converted to BT.2020/PQ; an HDR request with an SDR source fails setup instead of mislabelling the pixels. Static desktops refresh from retained encoder data without holding driver ring slots.
- **Step 2 capability negotiation.** SDR/HDR and chroma profiles are negotiated independently. DXGI/Vulkan probing runs in a bounded disposable child process, and negotiated quality, refresh, bitrate, loss telemetry and pacing settings reach the video worker. Compatible clients can negotiate session-local adaptive FEC and adaptive bitrate.
- **Quality and refresh controls.** Advanced settings expose bitrate, quality bias and refresh interval. The default refresh interval of **0** sends complete intra frames; conditional replenishment is an experimental opt-in for the exact client revisions documented in the testing guide. Frame budgets that exceed the current GameStream transport limits are rejected before capture.
- **Visible encoder status** ([#190](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/190), [#192](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/192)). Mission Control reports PyroWave after AV1 in the host status strip, with metadata that distinguishes compiled support from enabled, available advertisement.

PyroWave requires Vulkan 1.3 and the required Windows external-memory/keyed-mutex support on the capture adapter. No Vulkan SDK or LuminalVGD driver update is needed on the installed host. Start with the pinned Aurora client and the SDR/HDR acceptance steps in the [PyroWave testing guide](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/blob/6c397d2fc8d303d3444927834f1e43ea96e50e4a/docs/pyrowave.md). The 700 Mbps target excludes transport overhead; higher settings need sufficient network headroom. Full 10 Gbps transport and broad client/GPU validation remain outside this milestone.

## Borealis compatibility and GameStream responsiveness

- **Paired clients can identify the LuminalShine release** ([#199](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/199)). HTTPS `/serverinfo` appends `LuminalShineVersion` while preserving the GameStream `appversion` and `GfeVersion` values. The unauthenticated HTTP response is unchanged.
- **Unknown paths return one correctly framed response** ([#200](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/200), fixes [#194](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/issues/194)). The default handler no longer appends a second malformed response after the declared body. Clients still receive HTTP 200 with XML `status_code="404"`, followed by connection closure.
- **Long launches no longer occupy the HTTPS I/O thread** ([#203](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/203), fixes [#202](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/issues/202)). Launch, resume and cancel run in arrival order on one dedicated worker, allowing other clients' TLS handshakes and requests to proceed while display preparation and application startup run.
- **Shared state follows the new concurrency model.** Paired-client settings are protected and copied before use, codec capability reads use atomic values, and `/serverinfo` can report the starting application without waiting for its lifecycle lock. Shutdown finishes the active worker task and discards queued work. Regression tests cover response framing, version serialization, FIFO scheduling, responsiveness and pending-task shutdown.

### Contributor recognition

Special thanks to **[@magalz](https://github.com/magalz)** for contributing **[#199](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/199), [#200](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/200), and [#203](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/203)** to fix compatibility with **[Borealis](https://github.com/magalz/Borealis)** — an Android client based on Moonlight and tuned for LuminalShine. These contributions improve host identification, protocol response correctness and connection responsiveness for the wider Moonlight client ecosystem as well.

## Pairing, teardown and reconnect reliability

- **Pairing requests have distinct identities and bounded lifetimes** ([#188](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/188)). Client-specific request selection, exact four-digit PIN validation, retry-safe phase ownership and accurate final status in Mission Control prevent stale or repeated submissions from being confused with a completed pairing. Protocol secrets are redacted from request logging.
- **Launch preparation and last-session teardown are coordinated.** Generation checks keep an older session's cleanup from destroying a successor's display state. Launch failure, explicit cancellation and unclaimed-session expiry have deterministic rollback paths.
- **Cleanup restores session-wide state.** HDR, frame-limiter, RTSS, platform and runtime-override cleanup participate in the coordinated lifecycle. Independent watchdogs bound teardown phases, choosing the appropriate recovery path when cleanup cannot finish.
- **Regression coverage follows the lifecycle.** Pairing policy and UI tests cover retries and final outcomes; session tests cover admission, expiry, cancellation, cleanup transfer and watchdog behavior.

## Windows go to the correct virtual display

- **Exact-device window routing** ([#189](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/189)). In anchored-exclusive mode, the display helper receives the authoritative per-session LuminalVGD device identity and routes eligible application windows to that device instead of guessing from coordinates or the primary monitor. Shell, helper, tool and minimized windows are excluded, and placement is bounded to the target work area.
- **Event-driven placement with stale-work rejection.** Window events are coalesced, and topology/configuration generations prevent outdated work from moving windows after apply, revert, disconnect or delayed reapply.
- **Streaming startup does not wait for the router.** It arms after display topology, HDR and refresh preparation complete. Transitional or failed activation leaves routing inactive; it does not substitute another virtual or primary display. Placement remains asynchronous and teardown is bounded.

## Mission Control and application-library imports

- **Import a trusted `apps.json` from Library** ([4b4514e1](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/commit/4b4514e1cab28b39686c0316a10f7f63634817a2)). Select a file up to 5 MiB and confirm **Replace and import** to replace configured applications and their environment variables. Separately auto-synced catalogues are unaffected.
- **Validated, authenticated configuration writes.** Imports validate document structure and environment expansion, assign missing UUIDs, preserve supported extension fields, and save through the signed configuration writer. Protection of the configuration directory remains enabled. Only import trusted files: application and preparation commands can execute on the host. Programs and cover images are not transferred, so their paths must exist on this machine.
- **Clearer stream controls** ([#193](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/193)). HEVC and AV1 menus display their complete descriptions, and a zero maximum bitrate appears as **0 (Automatic)** without changing the saved numeric value.

## LuminalVGD driver

This prerelease keeps **[LuminalVGD v0.1.0-alpha.9](https://github.com/NortheBridge/LuminalVGD/releases/tag/v0.1.0-alpha.9)**, the signed package shipped with 26.09.1:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Driver version | **0.1.0.27** (`DriverVer 08/07/2026, 0.1.0.27`) |
| Protocol | **0.10** (handshake build 27, capabilities `0xfe5`) |
| Watchdog | 10-second lease watchdog |
| Signing | NortheBridge Foundation OV certificate, RFC 3161 timestamped |

Build 27 retains the D3D12 timeline-fence transport and teardown/drain protections described in 26.09.1. PyroWave and exact-device routing are host-side additions; neither requires a new driver package. Upgrading from 26.09.1 does not normally require replacing the bundled driver.

## Project, tests and release engineering

- **WebRTC and PyroWave are explicitly enabled in Windows release CI.** WebRTC's runtime is packaged alongside the application. Vulkan/glslang build dependencies support PyroWave shader generation, and Windows coverage builds compile PyroWave too.
- **Deterministic CI gates.** Release CI includes a PyroWave/connection-path gate, configuration consistency checks and a GameStream server-info readiness self-test. The general test suite retains its existing reporting behavior; a successful build is not a claim that every historical baseline test is green.
- **Stable Windows packaging** ([#206](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/206)). Install the optional libatomic runtime explicitly so upgrades retain the shipped DLL. MSI compatibility checks recognize truncated Vue content hashes while continuing to reject real component changes.
- **Reliable Windows linking** ([#188](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/188)). Clang/UCRT builds explicitly select lld, avoiding GNU ld COMDAT failures.
- **Deployment readiness checks** ([#191](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/191)). The reusable GameStream checker accepts string and byte-array HTTP bodies, validates server-info XML, accepts FREE or BUSY state, and uses a bounded 180-second default startup window.
- **Documentation refresh.** Read the Docs uses a charcoal-and-yellow design with slide-out navigation and a revised landing page. EPUB builds use the standard EPUB template, and configuration/PyroWave documentation covers imports, experimental controls, prerequisites and acceptance testing.
- **Release CI results** ([run](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/actions/runs/39492270592)): MSI upgrade compatibility, installer invariants, signature verification, GameStream health-check self-tests, PyroWave/connection-path tests and configuration consistency all passed. The advisory suite recorded **790 passed, 12 failed and 10 skipped** (812 total); failures concern an authentication error-text expectation, eight Playnite tests and three locale-consistency tests. This is not an all-tests-green release.
- **Local validation before the packaging-only fix:** the Windows application and production web UI built successfully, and 114 selected connection/session regressions passed. Live Moonlight/Borealis streaming was not exercised in that local run; PyroWave hardware acceptance remains as documented in its testing guide.

## Upgrading

- This is **26.10.0-beta.1**, a prerelease for testing. Install over 26.09.1 with the installer; settings, pairings and the existing LuminalVGD driver are retained.
- An active stream ends during the upgrade and can be restarted after the service returns.
- Hard-refresh Mission Control once (`Ctrl+F5`) if cached assets from 26.09.1 remain visible.
- WebRTC remains available from the **Play** page. PyroWave stays disabled until explicitly enabled and requires a compatible client; ordinary Moonlight sessions continue to use H.264, HEVC or AV1.

## Checksums

SHA-256:

```text
9059118bbd7a17aae602635bd4e55b07b34071700a4a46a5b268c859925775cf  LuminalShine_x64-debuginfo.7z
6cfc3e5d5e6a8c7531d4697d04cf9de5644537894c84c80b5cca15605846b010  LuminalShine_x64-installer.exe
8e32e3887788f1641c1f0b131ac36d6c1976a7d0c25a90b551e2f0958ecefaff  LuminalShine_x64-portable.zip
```

The same hashes are attached as **SHA256SUMS**.

**Full changes:** [`6c377335…e2662a44`](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/compare/6c377335d38c180537b3909866c11789a3a0b216...e2662a44f8533df85dad163c4e947945e67d7fcd)

# LuminalShine 26.09.1

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Bundled virtual display driver: LuminalVGD v0.1.0-alpha.9**  
> Signed driver **0.1.0.27** · protocol **0.10** · Build **27** — unchanged from 26.09.0.

LuminalShine 26.09.1 is the release where the browser streaming path becomes part of the official Windows build. WebRTC is now compiled in, its runtime is shipped with every installer and portable archive, and a fresh build fetches a checksum-pinned wrapper directly from the NortheBridge repository. This release also makes browser sessions and Moonlight sessions hand off cleanly, tears abandoned browser sessions down, fixes two display-helper races behind slow starts and quick reconnects, and closes several Mission Control polish gaps.

## WebRTC ships in the official Windows build

- **WebRTC is enabled by default on Windows** ([#176](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/176), fixes [#157](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/issues/157)). Previous official builds exposed the Play page while compiling the host-side WebRTC implementation out. Release CI now enables it explicitly, packages `libwebrtc.dll`, and stages the DLL beside the test executable as well.
- **The wrapper comes from a pinned NortheBridge release.** CMake downloads `libwebrtc-win-x64-release.zip` from `NortheBridge/libwebrtc` tag `luminalshine-m150.1`, verifies SHA-256 `45fec22b910b92b414da4a1fa65179baa4367e4db13c43aefcf55b36490d77a0`, and reuses the shared cache on later builds. A missing header or runtime DLL is a hard configuration error instead of a package that starts without its dependency.
- **Moonlight and browser capture are mutually exclusive.** A Moonlight launch preempts an existing browser session; a browser connection is refused while Moonlight is streaming or still connecting. The launch-pending latch spans the HTTP handler, RTSP hand-off and bounded connection window so two capture workers cannot divide the same LuminalVGD frame ring ([#176](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/176), [#180](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/180)).
- **Recovery keyframes are acknowledged at the WebRTC encoder boundary.** Browser sessions no longer log repeated recovery-IDR timeouts simply because the acknowledgement previously lived only in the RTSP sender.
- **Lost browser links now clean themselves up** ([#181](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/181)). The `luminalshine-m150.1` wrapper exposes peer and ICE state callbacks. A failed connection closes immediately; a disconnected connection gets a 10-second recovery window before the session, capture worker and virtual display are released. Short network hiccups and successful ICE restarts remain transparent.
- **Better browser-session diagnostics.** The host records negotiated video, the first accepted keyframe, data-channel and peer/ICE transitions, and 30-second egress windows; session counters are exposed through the WebRTC session API.
- **Esc reliably leaves fullscreen.** Holding Esc exits native fullscreen and the browser fallback mode, with an on-screen hold indicator and a one-time explanation.

WebRTC can still be disabled for a custom build with `-DSUNSHINE_ENABLE_WEBRTC=OFF`. The classic Moonlight path remains unchanged and is still the path to use when broad native-client compatibility is the priority.

## Display and reconnect reliability

- **Slow display-helper startup no longer loses a successful APPLY** ([#182](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/182)). The host previously gave up on the anonymous-pipe handshake after 500 ms, reconnected with the wrong protocol shape and then waited ten seconds for a reply the decoder could never recover. Display-helper connections now use one bounded, process-aware handshake and keep the APPLY transaction on the same connection.
- **Quick relaunches no longer race duplicate REVERT requests** ([#183](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/183)). Session cleanup and app-exit cleanup now serialize the duplicate check with the transactional restore, preventing a second helper from starting against an already-restored topology. If a helper genuinely exits during the activation APPLY, the host restarts it and retries once instead of spending the full activation timeout on a dead process.
- These fixes apply to both Moonlight and browser sessions because they harden the shared Windows display-management path.

## Mission Control polish

- **The LuminalShine logo loads everywhere** ([#184](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/184)). The reserved `/images` route now serves the branded logo used by the shell, login page and logged-out screen. Route coverage prevents future Web UI image references from silently becoming broken images.
- **The YUV 4:4:4 switch now reflects and preserves the saved value** ([#184](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/184), follow-up for [#178](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/issues/178)). Configuration booleans returned as strings are normalized consistently, fixing the same class of stale-toggle problem for Steam Library, Lossless Scaling and other boolean-backed settings.
- **Configuration hot-apply respects active WebRTC sessions.** Autosave and app-lifecycle paths now defer global configuration replacement while either a Moonlight or browser stream is active, instead of checking only RTSP sessions.

## LuminalVGD driver

This release keeps **LuminalVGD v0.1.0-alpha.9**, the same signed package shipped with 26.09.0:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Driver version | **0.1.0.27** (`DriverVer 08/07/2026, 0.1.0.27`) |
| Protocol | **0.10** (handshake build 27, capabilities `0xfe5`) |
| Watchdog | 10-second lease watchdog |
| Signing | NortheBridge Foundation OV certificate, RFC 3161 timestamped |

Build 27 carries the D3D12 timeline-fence transport used by Direct-to-Encode and the teardown/drain protections that prevent the Windows indirect-display host from being terminated during monitor departure, RDP/console transitions or a delayed ring hand-off. Because the bundled driver has not changed, upgrading from 26.09.0 does not normally require a driver replacement or restart page.

## Project, tests and release engineering

- Windows release builds now compile and package WebRTC from the checksum-pinned NortheBridge wrapper, and the test binary receives the same runtime DLL.
- WebRTC exclusivity, peer-link liveness, display-helper connection policy, duplicate-revert suppression, static image routes and configuration boolean coercion all have regression coverage.
- The signed release path uses SSL.com eSigner with a maintained Java 11 trust store while retaining strict TLS validation and post-sign Authenticode verification ([#185](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/185)).

## Upgrading

- Install over 26.09.0 with the installer; settings, pairings and the LuminalVGD driver are kept.
- An active stream ends during the upgrade and can be restarted after the service returns.
- Hard-refresh the Web UI once (`Ctrl+F5`) if a browser still shows cached assets from 26.09.0.
- Existing Moonlight clients continue to pair and connect as before. Browser streaming is now available from the **Play** page without a custom build.

# LuminalShine 26.09.0

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Bundled virtual display driver: LuminalVGD v0.1.0-alpha.9**  
> Signed driver **0.1.0.27** · protocol **0.10** · Build **27** — unchanged from 26.08.4.

LuminalShine 26.09.0 is the **Mission Control** release: the Web UI has been rebuilt from the ground up as a single pane of glass, with everything you used to check across Dashboard, Clients, Applications, Troubleshooting and About visible from one Overview and every detail opening in place. Under the hood it closes the NVENC crash family that hit RTX 30-series (Ampere) hosts, keeps the streamed cursor steady on the current Windows Insider build, unlocks 5.1 / 7.1 audio over WebRTC, and teaches the installer to say when Windows needs a restart.

Thanks to **[@magalz](https://github.com/magalz)** for the RTX 30-series fixes in this release — see *Encoder reliability* below.

## Mission Control — the new Web UI

Open the Web UI after upgrading and you land on a different application. The design goal was one screen that tells you the state of the host at a glance, with details and settings that open beside what you are looking at instead of on another page.

**The shell**

- A 56 px icon rail on the left replaces the top navigation: **Overview, Stream, Play, Library, Clients, Display, Settings, Diagnostics**. Old bookmarks keep working — every legacy route redirects to its new home.
- An always-on **host strip** across the top shows host status, active encoder, display backend, network port and address family, session monitor state and any open incidents, plus the global save indicator.
- **Global search** in the strip finds pages, settings sections, individual settings, apps and paired clients from one box. An app hit opens the Library filtered to it, a client hit opens that client, and free text jumps straight to the matching setting.
- A right-hand **inspector column** carries the details, editors and actions for whatever is selected on the page. On narrow screens it becomes a slide-in drawer with a floating toggle; Escape closes it.
- New design tokens throughout: dark chrome, a single gold accent, IBM Plex Sans and Mono. Bootstrap is gone from every rebuilt page.

**Overview** replaces the Dashboard. Host identity, live session, capture health, recent sessions, connected clients and a "Needs attention" list of everything the old page surfaced as banners, all on one screen.

**Stream** (replaces Stats). A session list on the left, the selected session in the middle with a live/ended header, six headline numbers, a range selector (full session / 3 / 5 / 15 min) and three charts — encode latency, actual FPS and network throughput. The inspector holds identity, connection and quality rows, and lets you disconnect an active session or delete an ended one.

**Library** (replaces Applications). A cover grid with source filters (Playnite, Steam, custom), a text filter, Playnite integration status with a force-sync action, and the full app editor for launch, prep commands, display overrides and frame generation.

**Clients** (replaces Client Management). A table of paired devices with device, display, status and last-seen columns; the inspector edits the selected client's display and stream overrides or pairs a new device by PIN. API tokens live on the same page.

**Display** (replaces the LuminalVGD Control Panel). Driver card (bundled vs installed version, signature, status), the host's physical and virtual outputs, the four configuration groups (backend and sessions, disconnect and pause behaviour, modes and refresh, HDR), the driver transition prompt, golden-snapshot export and delete, and an inspector that runs the driver diagnostic automatically, with copy and restart-driver actions.

**Settings**. A left sub-navigation of the nine sections replaces the accordion; the active section is in the URL, and search results land on and highlight the exact field. The three separate save surfaces are collapsed into one **Changes** panel in the inspector: last save time, pending state, validation, a **needs-restart** list of the settings that require a service restart (port, address family, UPnP, certificate and key), the recently changed values with before/after, **Discard pending** and **Apply & restart**. Settings still auto-save; the panel simply tells you what happened.

**Diagnostics** (merges Troubleshooting, Logs and About). Health cards for the GPU and display stack (TDR count, stack state, last reset with detail), the capture and render stack (engine, DLSS / DLAA / Frame Generation detection, tips) and drivers and buses; header actions for export logs, force close and restart; the crash-dump alert with a one-click bundle export; and the log viewer with a source selector, chunked search with context snippets, follow-the-tail and per-level tinting. The inspector holds the copyable host report (plain text or Markdown, ready to paste into a bug report) and the five reset actions. The full About page remains one click away.

**Web links** now point at the Moonlight community Discord invite, with a note that LuminalShine lives in the server's Experimental category.

## Encoder reliability — RTX 30-series and every NVENC host

- **AV1 probing on GPUs without AV1 encode** ([#156](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/156), by [@magalz](https://github.com/magalz)). On RTX 30-series / Ampere hosts (an RTX 3080 Ti in the report) the NVENC probe attempted AV1, the driver rejected it, and the failure took H.264 and HEVC down with it — the host fell back to software encoding or crashed outright. The capability check now knows which NVIDIA generations encode AV1, with regression tests for Turing, Ampere, Ada and future device-ID ranges. Fixes [#147](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/issues/147).
- **Safe teardown of a never-initialized NVENC session** ([#159](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/159)). The crash behind the Ampere report was general: tearing down a session that was opened but never initialized unregistered an async event that had never been registered. That path is now closed for every codec, and the terminate handler's one-shot guard no longer turns a second fault into a silent exit.
- **A faulting codec no longer costs the whole encoder** ([#162](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/162)). When one codec's probe faults, the next pass skips only that codec instead of discarding NVENC entirely and dropping to libx264 forever.

## Capture

- **Cursor held visible while the OS visibility flag flaps** ([#167](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/167)). Windows 11 Insider build 29648 has a documented bug that makes the mouse cursor blink; the streamed cursor mirrored it. A short hold on the visibility flag keeps the streamed cursor steady without adding latency on healthy builds.

## Audio

- **5.1 and 7.1 over WebRTC** ([#165](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/165)). Surround was previously only available on the classic Moonlight path: browsers never offer multichannel Opus, so a WebRTC session could only ever be stereo. The built-in web client now adds a multichannel Opus payload to its own offer, the host selects it and restates the channel layout from the same table the native encoder uses, and a Stereo / 5.1 / 7.1 selector in the WebRTC session settings is saved with the client profile. If the peer cannot take surround the session falls back to stereo, says so in the UI, and downmixes with proper ITU-R BS.775 coefficients instead of dropping the centre channel and most of the dialogue with it. 5.1 is the well-trodden path in Chrome; treat 7.1 as the less exercised of the two.

## Installer

- **Restart page when the LuminalVGD driver is updated** ([#172](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/172)). Some hosts keep the previous driver image loaded until Windows restarts. When an install or upgrade moves the bundled driver to a newer version, the installer no longer closes itself; it ends on a page naming both versions with **Restart Now** and **Restart Later**, confirms a deferral, and registers the pending restart with Windows either way (exit code 3010 for silent installs, so winget and management tools report it). Upgrading from 26.08.3 does not change the driver, so this page will not appear on this upgrade.

## Project, tests and CI

- The README gains a **Project Contributors** section ([#174](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/174)), starting with [@magalz](https://github.com/magalz).
- The Windows coverage gate reports real data again ([#160](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/160)), and the test-only Simple-Web-Server client use-after-free that crashed the coverage build was root-caused and fixed at the source ([#164](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/164)).
- The MSI upgrade-compatibility baseline advanced to the 26.09.0 table set ([#175](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/175)); only the renamed Web UI asset components moved, and the invariants gate (UpgradeCode, services, pinned component GUIDs) is unchanged.

## Upgrading

- Install over 26.08.4 with the installer; settings, pairings and the driver are kept. A stream that is active when you upgrade ends and can be restarted a minute or two later.
- The Web UI's old URLs redirect. Hard-refresh once (Ctrl+F5) if the browser shows the previous interface from cache.
- Nothing in this release changes the streaming protocol; existing Moonlight clients pair and connect as before.

```

```

# LuminalShine 26.08.4

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Bundled virtual display driver: LuminalVGD v0.1.0-alpha.9**  
> Signed driver **0.1.0.27** · protocol **0.10** · Build **27** · driver build date **August 7, 2026**

LuminalShine 26.08.4 is a stable Windows reliability and documentation release. It improves behavior under heavy GPU-memory pressure, restores the preferred NVIDIA driver-settings path with compatibility fallback, makes forced shutdowns cleaner when the graphics stack is wedged, and brings the public architecture documentation in line with the implementation—including the existing AMD AMF hardware-encoding pipeline.

## Highlights

- **VRAM paging-stall mitigation:** LuminalShine now maintains a cooperative `IDXGIAdapter3` video-memory reservation for each active adapter. The reservation tracks the process working set with bounded headroom, observes Windows VidMm budget changes, and logs material usage, budget, reservation, and over-budget transitions.
- **Paging-storm pressure relief:** repeated large budget moves are recognized as a paging storm. Capture temporarily halves its claim rate while VidMm is moving allocations in bulk, then automatically returns to full rate after the budget settles. This reduces LuminalShine's contribution to GPU/PCIe stalls during high-pressure game transitions.
- **NVIDIA power-profile compatibility:** the official `NvAPI_DRS_SetSetting` interface is preferred again so legacy DRS settings—including the high-performance power-state pin—work on current R610-era drivers. The NVIDIA-App-era interface remains available as a call-time fallback.
- **Cleaner recovery from wedged shutdowns:** if orderly termination cannot complete within ten seconds, LuminalShine now exits without deliberately generating a crash dump in the middle of a graphics-stack collapse; the service wrapper can restart it cleanly.
- **AMD AMF architecture reference:** a transparent 1672 × 941 PNG at [`mmd/AMD_AMF_PIPELINE.png`](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/blob/26.08.4/mmd/AMD_AMF_PIPELINE.png) documents the already-implemented FFmpeg/AMF hardware path, including D3D11 capture/input, runtime probing, H.264/AVC, HEVC, and AV1 selection, color/HDR handling, low-latency controls, safeguards, hardware/driver requirements, and encoded-frame delivery.

## AMD AMF support in this release

AMD AMF hardware encoding was already implemented in LuminalShine and remains fully available in 26.08.4 through the FFmpeg AMF encoders. At startup LuminalShine probes the installed AMD AMF runtime (`amfrt64.dll`) and per-codec capabilities, binds AMF to a D3D11 device, and exposes H.264/AVC, HEVC, and AV1 when supported by the installed AMD GPU and driver. The new diagram makes that implemented path easy to audit; this release does not replace the encoder implementation with documentation-only behavior.

## Documentation and project presentation

This release contains the complete Claude-assisted documentation series merged after 26.08.3:

- **README modernization ([#150](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/150)):** refreshed the project overview and feature list; linked the official LuminalShine product page; described LuminalVGD as the shipped first-party virtual-display backend; updated Windows system, hardware, software, development, WebRTC, encoder, Vue/Tailwind, WiX 7, WinGet, portable-package, licensing, and contributor information.
- **Correct documentation URL ([#151](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/151)):** replaced the stale documentation address with the official [`appdocs.northebridge.com/projects/luminalshine/en/latest/`](https://appdocs.northebridge.com/projects/luminalshine/en/latest/) site.
- **Direct-to-Encoder architecture ([#152](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/152)):** corrected the capture description to show DWM rendering into LuminalVGD, frames and HDR metadata crossing the shared-texture VGD ring, and the D3D11, D3D11-on-D3D12, and native D3D12 encode paths. WGC is documented as the seamless mid-stream fallback with active D2E restoration and DXGI Desktop Duplication as the last-resort tier.
- **Remove obsolete SudoVDA references ([#153](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/153)):** aligned the README with the current product by identifying LuminalVGD as the sole virtual-display backend.
- **AMD AMF pipeline chart ([#155](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/155)):** added the transparent PNG architecture chart covering the implemented AMF pipeline, supported codecs, runtime/capability probing, safeguards, and requirements.

## Windows stability work

The VRAM stability change in [#154](https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/pull/154) includes:

- one idempotent, process-lifetime VRAM keeper per adapter LUID;
- cooperative reservation sizing based on current local-memory use plus 12.5% headroom, clamped to Windows' available reservation budget;
- reservation hysteresis to avoid churn from ordinary frame-to-frame allocation movement;
- event-driven VidMm budget monitoring with a polling fallback;

# LuminalShine 26.08.3

LuminalShine 26.08.3 is a performance-focused release: it removes a hard ~21 fps delivery ceiling that affected high-resolution HDR sessions and cuts standing capture-to-send latency from ~145 ms to ~6 ms, restoring full client-requested frame rates (verified live at 3456×2160@120 YUV 4:4:4 10-bit HDR: 119 fps sustained). It bundles the signed **LuminalVGD v0.1.0-alpha.9** (driver 0.1.0.27, protocol 0.10, Build 27, driver build date 08/07/2026).

The root cause was OS timing behavior on current Windows builds: timed waits that expire cost a full ~15.6 ms timer quantum even at 0 ms timeouts, and timer-resolution raises can be silently ignored for windowless background service processes. Two per-frame loops each stacked three quanta (3 × 15.6 ms ≈ the observed 47 ms/frame cadence). All hot-path waits now use quantization-immune primitives, and the pipeline self-reports its timing health in every log.

## Highlights

- **Full-rate frame delivery:** the capture ring poll and the egress loop's sideband event checks no longer pay timer quanta; sessions deliver at the client-requested rate (21 → 119 fps in the field) with capture-to-send latency of a few milliseconds.
- **Real-time worker timing profile:** the isolated capture/encode worker raises timer resolution, opts out of background power throttling, runs at high priority (restoring parity with the pre-isolation architecture), and logs its measured sleep quantum at startup — support bundles now prove which timing regime a host is in.
- **Stream-ordered CUDA interop (YUV 4:4:4 10-bit):** the per-frame map/copy/unmap sequence is enqueued on a dedicated non-blocking stream with polled completion and a bounded 1 s deadline that fails into normal session recovery instead of blocking until GPU reset. Falls back to the synchronous path automatically when unavailable.
- **Pipeline health telemetry:** one 30-second line per stage — capture cadence (driver-published vs host-claimed frames), encode cycle, NVENC phases, worker egress, and broadcast cycle — attributes any future delivery ceiling to a single stage from a standard log.
- **Attributable capture reinits:** display-stack-triggered encoder rebuilds now log their trigger instead of restarting silently.
- **Wider worker video pipe:** the worker-to-host video channel grows from 64 KiB to 4 MiB, decoupling encode cadence from the host reader's drain cadence.
- **Bundled LuminalVGD v0.1.0-alpha.9:** signed driver 0.1.0.27, protocol 0.10 fence-only transport, teardown/drain fixes for stall-free monitor departure.

## Also in this release (26.08.2 → 26.08.3)

- Strict-client session startup: encoder prewarm at launch and a bounded ANNOUNCE hold for clients with tight connection budgets (Xbox, webOS).
- Decoder-safe egress QoS: predictive frames after a lost packet are withheld until a fresh IDR; bitrate-aware wire pacing shapes bursts to the negotiated rate.
- LuminalVGD host resilience: deferred ring-generation binding, control-device self-heal after I/O failure, and clean WGC pivot when a ring is unavailable.
- Display helper: calmer apply verification and pre-capture modeset ordering.
- Outbound TLS floor raised to 1.2; SSLv2/v3 disabled on GameStream HTTPS.
- Mailbox and process-lifecycle hardening in the session core.
- Modernized streaming architecture diagrams in the documentation.
- Release tooling: the MSI upgrade-compatibility oracle now normalizes the Upgrade table's version-bearing fields, so version bumps no longer trip the gate while UpgradeCode and upgrade semantics remain enforced.

# LuminalShine 26.08.2

LuminalShine 26.08.2 is a stability-focused release for direct-to-encode streaming. It introduces a stricter ownership boundary between LuminalVGD's display surfaces and the hardware encoder, moves capture/encoding into an isolated worker process, and bundles the signed LuminalVGD v0.1.0-alpha.8 (driver version 0.1.0.24, protocol 0.10, Build 24).

The goal of this architecture is to prevent a stalled, replaced, or retired indirect-display swapchain from wedging LuminalShine's main process or the Windows display stack. Native D3D12 encoding remains available; this release does not replace D3D12 with a lower-fidelity capture path and does not inject hooks into games.

## Highlights

- **Isolated capture and encode worker:** video capture and hardware encoding now run outside the main LuminalShine process. A capture/encoder failure can be detected and recovered without taking the control, audio, input, or session-management process down with it.
- **LuminalVGD surfaces are decoupled from encoder lifetime:** the worker copies each accepted VGD frame into a bounded pool of worker-owned surfaces, releases the VGD ring slot, and only then submits the worker-owned resource to NVENC, AMF, or QSV.
- **Immutable Build 24 fence transport:** direct VGD capture uses the protocol 0.10 fence-only contract. A ring generation is admitted only after stable metadata snapshots, and synchronization semantics are not downgraded inside the same generation.
- **Deterministic failure handling:** a broken or inconsistent ring generation is marked dead and rebuilt instead of being silently reused through a weaker synchronization path.
- **Safer fallback boundary:** WGC/DDA fallback is confined to the isolated worker. Fallback capture cannot retain or reinterpret a retired LuminalVGD surface.
- **Native D3D12 retained:** supported D3D12-to-NVENC operation remains available alongside D3D11 NVENC, AMD AMF, and Intel Quick Sync paths.
- **Signed Build 24 driver included:** the installer bundles the current stable LuminalVGD alpha.8 package and verifies its pinned SHA-256 during the release build.

## Direct-to-encode reliability

The direct path now observes a strict resource-ownership sequence:

1. LuminalVGD publishes a completed frame and fence value through the protocol 0.10 ring.
2. The isolated worker waits for the advertised completion fence.
3. The frame is copied into one of four bounded worker-owned surfaces.
4. The LuminalVGD ring slot is released immediately after the copy completes.
5. The worker-owned surface is converted or encoded through the selected hardware backend.
6. If the ring generation changes, the previous generation is retired without allowing encoder work to retain its surfaces.

This prevents encoder back-pressure from extending the lifetime of IddCx-owned swapchain resources. It also removes the unsafe condition where NVENC could still reference a surface while Windows or LuminalVGD was deleting or reassigning the corresponding swapchain.

## Worker recovery and admission controls

- Direct capture waits for two mutually consistent ring snapshots before admitting a new generation.
- Ring admission is bounded to six seconds so an unusable generation cannot block session startup indefinitely.
- Worker-owned frame storage is bounded to four surfaces, limiting queue growth and making overload behavior predictable.
- A failed worker can be terminated and recreated without restarting the main LuminalShine service.
- Capture fallback is selected inside the worker and does not weaken the active VGD generation's synchronization contract.

## Display and client behavior

- Client-requested resolution, refresh rate, HDR, and chroma behavior remain controlled by the negotiated stream configuration.
- HEVC 4:4:4 HDR workflows remain supported where the client and encoder support them.
- Native frame-generation refresh handling remains available without requiring a global frame-generation override.
- LuminalShine does not hook a game's `Present`/`Present1` path; D3D11 and D3D12 games continue to render through the Windows compositor and LuminalVGD display pipeline.

## State and recovery hardening

This release includes the state-file and temporary-state handling improvements introduced during the 26.08 series. Session recovery tolerates interrupted temporary writes, avoids treating stale temporary files as authoritative state, and restores display topology through the normal recovery path.

## Bundled LuminalVGD

- Release: **LuminalVGD v0.1.0-alpha.8**
- Driver file version: **0.1.0.24**
- Protocol: **0.10**
- Driver build: **24**
- Package: `LuminalVGD-v0.1.0-alpha.8-x64.zip`
- Package SHA-256: `1cbe52890c732e5dfb6d2455d9035eb4c7881ab19dd49d89343b8b1fdbf807c2`

The LuminalShine release workflow downloaded this exact package, checked the pinned digest, and validated its signatures before producing the installer.

## Installation and upgrade

Use `LuminalShine_x64-installer.exe` for a normal installation or upgrade. The installer and bundled driver may require elevation. Reboot if Windows requests it after replacing the display driver; otherwise, restart LuminalShine before beginning a new test session.

The MSI upgrade-compatibility and invariant gates passed for this release. Existing LuminalShine installations using the same UpgradeCode are upgraded in place, while service identities, component GUIDs, custom-action contracts, and installer feature conditions remain protected by CI.

The portable ZIP is also provided for advanced testing. Driver installation and service integration still require the installer or equivalent elevated setup.

## Validation performed by release CI

- Downloaded and checksum-verified LuminalVGD alpha.8 Build 24
- Validated bundled driver signatures
- Built LuminalShine with the UCRT64 Windows toolchain
- Signed application executables
- Built and signed the MSI and bootstrapper installer
- Verified Authenticode signatures on staged release artifacts
- Passed MSI upgrade-compatibility comparison
- Passed MSI invariant validation
- Passed Windows unit tests and configuration-consistency checks
- Produced installer, portable, and debug-information artifacts from merge commit `b46405043aa5f6951083453c4123710266408c73`

## Release assets

- `LuminalShine_x64-installer.exe` — signed installer and recommended download
- `LuminalShine_x64-portable.zip` — portable application package
- `LuminalShine_x64-debuginfo.7z` — debugging symbols for crash and hang investigation

## Notes and limitations

- Recovery isolation reduces the blast radius of capture/encoder failures; it cannot prevent an independent GPU driver or operating-system TDR.
- Hardware codec, 10-bit, HDR, and 4:4:4 availability still depend on the GPU, driver, client, and negotiated codec profile.
- Do not replace the bundled driver DLL or catalog independently. Windows driver package integrity and signing must remain intact.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/NortheBridge/luminalshine/compare/26.08.1...26.08.2
